Cipher garden // plg-stego

Nine ways to write a message where the drawing is the code: tiles, mazes, a space-filling thread, ridgelines, pigpen, constellations, a cipher disk, a reversible automaton and knotwork. Everything here decodes by eye, and every export is checked by reading the drawing back.

Starting points
Message

Pigpen and constellations draw letters, so they ignore "bits as". Classical ciphers are historical puzzles, not modern security.

Method
Hiding

Scattered bits follow UTP's seeded route, so only the key finds them. Constellations use the setting for decoy stars.

Shading
Caption and key
Paper

Split export writes one SVG per pen, numbered in plotting order, each with the same corner ticks. Machine marks let the plot decoder find the page and read how it was made; turn them off for a gallery copy. Retrofit: set everything exactly as the plot was made, choose retrofit, export each pen, then plot only the marks file onto the finished sheet in the same place on the mat.

drawing

Bits come from the UNRAVEL THE PURLOINED engine at repo commit dev (five-bit, Bacon, Morse, the classical ciphers and the seeded scatter route); drawing, fills and hidden lines are the shared PLG core. Ridgelines use vector hidden lines: each line is cut where a line in front of it rises over it. Pens: black 0.4 outlines, black 0.3 shading, a text pen, and an answer key pen.
